target_customer: Engineering and data-science teams at logistics, delivery and operations companies that build routing, scheduling and other decision (optimization) models
problem: Teams that build optimization and decision models (routing, assignment, scheduling) lacked software-engineering tooling to test, simulate, deploy and monitor them; the founders built such tooling at Grubhub.
business_model: B2B SaaS, per seat (pricing unpublished at seed in 2020), later a hosted DecisionOps platform with integrations to third-party solvers

founders.name: Carolyn Mooney
founders.background_notes: With O'Neil led a team of about 40 at Grubhub that built simulations to test delivery decision models (TechCrunch 2020-05). Described by YC as a systems engineer and analyst.

founders.name: Ryan O'Neil
founders.background_notes: YC bio: works in optimization and decision science (integer programming, constraint programming, decision diagrams); prefers Go.

technical_complexity.rationale: Core was a solver plus a simulation framework (Hop and Dash) for decision models, requiring operations-research expertise that the founders built at Grubhub.

defensibility.rationale: Once models are deployed and tested on the platform, teams face integration costs; the core solver and tooling are specialist work, but open solvers existed. Rating is the author's judgement from the product description.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; Gurobi and AMPL became integration partners (2024) and NVIDIA cuOpt was added as a solver; FICO acquired the company in May 2026.

market_need_then: The founders' own experience at Grubhub, where a team of about 40 simulated and tuned delivery decision models, showed the need (TechCrunch 2020-05). No customer or spend data was published at the seed round.

branding.domain_note: Company uses nextmv.io; history of any .com not sourced.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, developer-facing (docs, CLI, SDK blog posts)

brand_strength.rationale: CEO says the name is pronounced 'next move' but they are not picky, implying a pronunciation ambiguity; no evidence of mascot, community or brand press. Early products Hop and Dash had no sourced naming story.

outcome_analysis: Nextmv started from the founders' Grubhub work on testing and optimizing delivery decision models, raised $2.7M seed (May 2020) and $8M Series A (closed Dec 2020, announced Feb 2021) from FirstMark-led investors, and positioned itself as DecisionOps tooling around third-party solvers rather than as a competing solver. It stayed a roughly 22-person company and was acquired by FICO in May 2026 (terms undisclosed), a strategic exit that folds its experimentation and observability into the FICO Platform.
notes: Total raised conflicts across aggregators (PitchBook $22.7M, yespress about $19.3M, CB Insights $14.34M); TechCrunch said seed brought total to $3.4M, so earlier money may exist; only the two sourced rounds recorded. Series A closed Dec 2020 per company blog, announced 2021-02-09. Acquisition date 2026-05-18 is from PitchBook via search snippet; Faegre Drinker notice confirms completion; nextmv blog 'now part of FICO' returned 404. The seed and Series A coverage (TechCrunch, VentureBeat) names no competitors and no dated competitor source was found, so the list is empty. Name origin not found in any source.
